title: 9 Best Creative Agencies in San Francisco for 2026
summary: The 9 best creative agencies in San Francisco, with every location taken from the firm's own site and an honest note where no street address is published.
body_markdown:
**Key takeaways:**


- The best creative agencies in san francisco for campaigns are not the same firms as its design studios or UX shops, and this list covers only the first group.
- Only half the agencies here publish a street address. Where one does not, we say so rather than guessing a neighborhood.
- San Francisco creative talent is expensive by design. Federal figures put average annual pay in the city's advertising and PR sector at $168,086 across 428 establishments.
- Three of the four published addresses on this list sit on Battery Street. The city's agency cluster is smaller and more concentrated than the search results suggest.


Search for an SF creative agency and you get three different businesses wearing one label: advertising agencies that make campaigns, design studios that make brand systems and interfaces, and marketing firms that buy media.


This list is about the first group: the creative agencies San Francisco companies hire when they need an idea, a campaign and the work to run it, rather than a design system or a product interface. Everyday production is a separate purchase again, and our own[graphic](https://www.awesomic.com/graphic) work sits on that side of the line.


Awesomic is first, and we should be clear about why: we are not a San Francisco advertising agency. We are a design subscription, included here because a great many companies searching this term need creative production rather than a campaign. Where that is not what you need, the eight agencies below are the answer and we say so in our own entry.


## What a San Francisco creative agency actually sells


An advertising or creative agency sells an idea plus the work to express it: the strategic insight, the campaign platform, and the films, print and social work that carry it. You are buying judgment and craft, priced against the media budget behind it.


That is a different transaction from buying design capacity. A campaign agency will not be your day-to-day partner for the fifty small assets your marketing calendar generates, and asking it to be is how retainers get expensive without anyone feeling well served.


The San Francisco market has a particular character worth knowing. It is smaller than New York's, heavily weighted toward technology clients, and unusually concentrated geographically. Three of the four agencies below that publish a street address are on Battery Street, within a few blocks of each other.


Separating this list from its neighbors matters too. A creative agency San Francisco buyers hire for campaigns is not the same business as a design studio, which is why we keep a separate roundup of[design agencies in San Francisco](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/design-agencies-in-san-francisco) rather than merging the two.

### Awesomic


**Best for:** Ongoing creative production


**Overview:** We are the odd entry here and it is worth saying plainly. Awesomic is not an advertising agency and we do not make campaigns. We are a design subscription that supplies the production work a campaign generates and the everyday creative a marketing team runs through.


Companies usually need both, at different moments. You hire one of the agencies below for the idea, then discover that executing it across every channel, plus the ordinary calendar of decks, landing pages and social assets, is a separate and continuous problem.


That second problem is ours. A vetted designer is matched to you, usually inside a day, and the work runs on a monthly fee rather than a scoped project. Customers rate us 4.9 on Trustpilot and the same on Google Play, which in a category that publishes almost nothing is at least a number you can check.


**Filta** , a Y Combinator company building an NFT marketplace for face filters, is a fair illustration of the creative range involved. It was founded by **Chris Horne** , an Emmy and Peabody award winner who previously worked at Pixar, Oculus and Facebook, and the engagement covered web design and the mobile app rather than a single deliverable.


**Core services:**


- Campaign production across social, display and web
- Video and motion, from cutdowns to original pieces
- Brand and graphic assets applied consistently across channels
- Landing pages and microsites built in Webflow, Framer or WordPress
- Pitch decks and sales collateral
- Copy and QA on the All-in-One tier


**Industries served:** SaaS, consumer brands, marketplaces, fintech, agencies


**Pricing:** Graphic Pack costs $1,490 monthly. All-in-One, which adds copy and QA, costs $2,995. A $200 AI Designer tier sits below both and a quoted Dedicated Talent plan above them; quarterly billing removes 20%.


**Pros:** published rates in a category that quotes everything, production capacity without a retainer, works alongside an agency rather than replacing it, matched in about a day


**Cons:** we do not create campaigns, media strategy or advertising ideas, so for a brand platform you want one of the eight agencies below


**Engagement model:** Subscribe, get matched, and brief through the app. Many clients run us in parallel with a campaign agency rather than instead of one.


**How to run us alongside an agency:**


1. Book a demo and describe the production load your campaigns create.
2. Pick a tier sized to that monthly volume.
3. Share the campaign's brand and creative guidelines.
4. Send the adaptations and everyday assets to us, keeping the agency on the idea.
5. Scale the tier up around launches and down between them.


**Why it belongs on a San Francisco creative agencies list:** Because a real share of the people searching this term need creative output rather than a campaign, and hiring an agency for that is an expensive way to find out.


**Final verdict:** The right partner for continuous creative production. For the idea itself, keep reading.


## Keep the agency
on the big idea


We are not an ad agency. We produce what a campaign leaves behind: the cutdowns, adaptations, landing pages and everyday assets, priced as a subscription rather than a retainer.


[Get started](https://www.awesomic.com/pricing)[Book demo](https://www.awesomic.com/demo)

### AKQA


**Overview:** A global digital and creative agency with deep San Francisco roots, working across brand campaigns, digital experience and product, and one of the few firms here operating at genuine international scale.


**Core services:**


- Brand campaigns and integrated creative
- Digital experience and product design
- Innovation and technology-led brand work


**Industries served:** Technology, automotive, sport, consumer, luxury


**Published location:** 44 Montgomery Street, San Francisco, CA 94104


**Pricing:** No published rate. Engagements are scoped, and this is enterprise-scale work.


**Pros:** operates at global scale with local presence, unusually strong at the intersection of brand and technology, publishes a verifiable San Francisco address


**Cons:** no published pricing, oriented to large brand budgets, and a small company will not be its priority client


**Notable clients or work:** Publishes brand and digital work for major international clients across technology, automotive and sport.


**Where it wins:** Work where the brand idea and the technology that delivers it cannot be separated.


**Final verdict:** The most globally capable option here, priced accordingly.


### Duncan Channon


**Overview:** An independent San Francisco advertising agency with a long history in the city, known for brand campaigns and for a strong public-sector and social-issue practice alongside commercial work.


**Core services:**


- Advertising and brand campaign development
- Brand strategy and positioning
- Media planning and buying


**Industries served:** Consumer brands, public sector, technology, hospitality, healthcare


**Published location:** 22 Battery Street, San Francisco


**Pricing:** Nothing published; each engagement is scoped first.


**Pros:** genuinely independent rather than holding-company owned, publishes a verifiable Battery Street address, unusual depth in public-interest campaigns


**Cons:** no published pricing, a mid-sized agency so very large global rollouts are a stretch, and campaign work carries campaign budgets


**Notable clients or work:** Publishes advertising and brand campaign work spanning consumer and public-sector clients.


**Why buyers shortlist it:** Independence, which in practice means the people who pitch are the people who work on it.


**Final verdict:** One of the strongest independent options in the city.


### Pereira O'Dell


**Overview:** An agency built around storytelling and long-form branded content as much as conventional advertising, with offices in San Francisco and New York.


**Core services:**


- Integrated brand campaigns
- Branded content and long-form storytelling
- Brand platform and positioning work


**Industries served:** Technology, consumer, entertainment, automotive


**Published location:** 1265 Battery Street, San Francisco, with a New York office


**Pricing:** No published rate. Engagements are scoped per campaign.


**Pros:** genuine strength in narrative and content rather than only in short-form advertising, two-coast presence, publishes a San Francisco address


**Cons:** no published pricing, content-led approach needs a budget to match, and the two-office structure means asking who actually works on your account


**Notable clients or work:** Publishes integrated campaign and branded-content work for technology and consumer brands.


**Its real strength:** Campaigns that need to sustain attention for longer than thirty seconds.


**Final verdict:** A strong choice when the brief is a story rather than a message.


### Cutwater


**Overview:** An independent San Francisco agency with a craft-forward reputation, working across advertising, brand and content for a mix of consumer and category-challenger clients.


**Core services:**


- Advertising campaigns and brand platforms
- Content and social creative
- Brand identity and positioning work


**Industries served:** Consumer brands, food and beverage, technology, outdoor


**Published location:** 950 Battery St., Floor 4, San Francisco, CA 94111


**Pricing:** No published rate. Scoped per project or retainer.


**Pros:** independent and craft-led, publishes a full verifiable address, comfortable with challenger brands rather than only incumbents


**Cons:** no published pricing, smaller than the global firms so capacity is finite, and less depth in media and performance


**Notable clients or work:** Publishes advertising and brand campaign work across consumer categories.


**Best angle:** Brands that need to be noticed rather than merely present.


**Final verdict:** A sharp independent option for consumer campaign work.


### Argonaut


**Overview:** A full-service advertising agency operating from San Francisco and New York, covering strategy, creative and production for large consumer campaigns.


**Core services:**


- Full-service advertising and campaign development
- Brand strategy and creative platforms
- In-house production capability


**Industries served:** Automotive, consumer, retail, technology


**Published location:** Names San Francisco and New York on its own site; no street address published


**Pricing:** Not shown on the site. Work is sized per engagement.


**Pros:** genuinely full-service including production, two-coast capacity, experience with large consumer brands


**Cons:** neither a rate nor an office location appears on its site, and full-service scale is more than a startup needs


**Notable clients or work:** Publishes large-scale consumer advertising campaigns.


**Where it fits:** A national campaign that needs strategy, creative and production under one roof.


**Final verdict:** A serious option for a full campaign, with the caveat that you will have to ask where they actually sit.


### Traction


**Overview:** A San Francisco marketing agency positioned around moments that matter commercially, blending campaign creative with demand generation rather than treating them separately.


**Core services:**


- Campaign creative tied to commercial outcomes
- Demand generation and performance marketing
- Brand marketing and positioning


**Industries served:** Technology, SaaS, financial services, consumer


**Published location:** Names San Francisco on its own site; no street address published


**Pricing:** Absent from its pages, and quoted once scope is agreed.


**Pros:** connects creative to pipeline rather than leaving it at awareness, strong technology-sector experience, practical commercial framing


**Cons:** it names no fee and no address, and the performance orientation makes it less suited to pure brand work


**Notable clients or work:** Publishes campaign and demand-generation work for technology and financial-services clients.


**Why it made this list:** It answers the question most creative agencies dodge, which is what the work is supposed to do.


**Final verdict:** A good fit when creative has to be accountable to a number.


### Born & Bred


**Overview:** A creative marketing agency working from San Francisco and New York, weighted toward brand-led work for consumer and lifestyle clients.


**Core services:**

- Campaign creative across channels
- Content and social creative


**Industries served:** Consumer, lifestyle, food and beverage, technology


**Pricing:** Off the page. The number follows the scope.


**Pros:** brand-led rather than execution-led, two-coast presence, strong consumer and lifestyle sensibility


**Cons:** the site carries no rate card and no location, and it is less suited to technical B2B categories


**Notable clients or work:** Publishes brand and campaign work for consumer and lifestyle brands.


**The case for it:** Consumer brands that need a point of view before they need a campaign.

### Kindred


**Overview:** A full-service creative agency in San Francisco covering brand, campaign and content work for growth-stage and established clients.

- Full-service creative and campaign development

**Pros:** full-service across brand and campaign, comfortable with growth-stage budgets, San Francisco based


**Cons:** costs and whereabouts are both left off the site, and the bench is smaller than at the established firms


**Notable clients or work:** Publishes creative and brand campaign work across consumer and technology clients.


**Its niche:** Companies that have outgrown freelancers but cannot yet justify a large agency.


**Final verdict:** Worth a conversation for a first real agency relationship.


## Resizing banners
is not agency work


The agency owns the idea, the guidelines and the hero assets. We take the adaptations and the calendar on one subscription, so both sides do the work they are priced for.


One flat monthly fee · No per-project quotes · 500+ YC startups have worked with us


## How we chose these nine


The geography check did most of the work, and it removed more well-known names than it kept.


We required each firm to state its own location on its own site, and we recorded exactly what it publishes. Four publish a full street address. Four name San Francisco without one.


**Several genuinely well-known San Francisco agencies were dropped entirely** because we could not verify a location from their own pages. Their sites render location information in ways we could not read, and asserting a city from memory is the same class of error as guessing a price.


That is a stricter standard than most local roundups apply, and it is the main reason this list is nine rather than twenty. A directory will happily list forty firms as the best creative agencies in san francisco; most of that list serves the Bay Area rather than sitting in it.


We also kept the category boundary honest. Agencies whose actual business is product interfaces were left for our[UX design agencies](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/ux-design-agencies-in-san-francisco) roundup rather than folded in here to inflate the count.


## What creative work costs in San Francisco


Not one of the eight local agencies puts a fee on its site, so the useful information is what the market pays for the people doing the work.


Engagement How it is priced What drives the number


Campaign platform and creative Project fee Number of channels, production scope


Agency of record Monthly retainer Team size assigned to your account


Project-based creative Scoped fee Deliverable count and production complexity


Production only Per asset or monthly Volume and turnaround


Creative subscription Flat monthly The tier you choose


Local labor cost explains most of the difference between San Francisco and elsewhere. Federal figures for[San Francisco County](https://www.bls.gov/cew/) put the advertising, public relations and related services sector at **428 establishments** employing **5,663 people** at an **average annual wage of $168,086** in 2024. That average is what an agency's rate card has to cover.


That labor cost also explains the concentration. A sector with fewer than 500 establishments in the city is small, and the good ones are known to each other, which is why reputation travels faster here than the search results suggest. Buyers widening the search beyond the city usually end up comparing[creative design agencies](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/creative-design-agencies) nationally instead.


The broader picture is worth holding too. The Bureau of Economic Analysis reports that[arts and cultural production](https://www.bea.gov/data/special-topics/arts-and-culture) accounted for **4.2 percent of US GDP, or $1.17 trillion, in 2023** , growing **6.6 percent** in real terms against 2.9 percent for the wider economy. Creative work is a large and fast-growing part of the economy, which is why so many firms want the label.


## Choosing between them


Start with what you are actually buying. If you need an idea that will run across channels for a year, you want a campaign agency and you should be talking to four or five of the firms above. If you need work produced against an idea you already have, an agency retainer is an expensive way to get it.


The second question is who works on the account. At mid-sized independents the people in the pitch usually are the team; at larger firms they usually are not. That single question separates the experience of working with these San Francisco advertising agencies more than any capability difference does.


Finally, decide whether you need San Francisco at all. Proximity matters for work that requires frequent in-person collaboration and matters much less for everything else, and the premium is real. If what you need is category expertise rather than a postcode, our wider roundup of[full-service creative agencies](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/full-service-creative-agencies) is the better starting point.


## Working with an agency and a production partner together


The arrangement most marketing teams end up with is not one vendor but two: an agency for the thinking and a production partner for the volume.


That split works because the economics are different. An agency's team is priced for judgment, and using it to resize banners is a waste of both parties' time. A production partner is priced for throughput and has no opinion about your brand platform, which at that stage is exactly right.


Set the boundary explicitly. The agency owns the idea, the guidelines and the hero assets; the production partner owns adaptations, everyday assets and the calendar. Our own[video](https://www.awesomic.com/video) work sits almost entirely on that second side, and the teams who get the most from it are the ones who drew the line before the campaign launched.


## FAQ


### What do creative agencies in San Francisco actually do?


The creative agencies San Francisco buyers shortlist for this search develop advertising and brand campaigns: the strategic insight, the creative idea, and the films, social, print and digital work that carry it. That is distinct from design studios, which build brand systems and interfaces, and from media agencies, which plan and buy placement. Ask any firm which of the three it does before comparing proposals.


### How much do San Francisco creative agencies charge?


Every one of the eight quotes rather than publishes, and campaign work is scoped per engagement. What is verifiable is the cost base: federal data puts average annual pay in San Francisco's advertising and PR sector at $168,086, which is what agency rates have to cover. Expect project fees for campaigns and monthly retainers for ongoing agency-of-record relationships.


### Do I need an agency based in San Francisco?


Only if the work genuinely requires frequent in-person collaboration, or if local market knowledge is part of the brief. Plenty of companies hire a creative agency San Francisco clients rate without ever visiting the office. San Francisco carries a real cost premium, and for category expertise rather than proximity a firm elsewhere may serve you better. Decide which of the two you are buying before you filter by location.


### Why do so few agencies publish an address?


Post-2020 many creative agencies moved to distributed or hybrid working and stopped maintaining a public office listing. Four of the eight here name San Francisco without publishing a street address. It is not necessarily a warning sign, but it is worth asking where the team actually sits if you expect in-person sessions.


### What is the difference between a creative agency and a design agency?


An SF creative agency in the campaign sense sells ideas, measured by whether the work moves an audience. A design agency sells systems and craft: identity, interfaces, and the rules that keep them consistent, a distinction our roundup of[advertising design agencies](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/advertising-design-agencies) draws out further. Many companies need both at different times, and buying one expecting the other is the most common mismatch in this market.
